Britain's Civil Aviation Authority has issued a statement warning travelers of follow-on

Workers in New York City are removing rubble from the Brooklyn building collapse that killed
at least eight people on Wednesday.

Trucks have been hauling away large containers filled with rubble from the collapsed three-story
apartment building.

river cruise ship docked in New Orleans.
Officials are describing the emergency response as textbook.
Dozens of people were hurled into the water as the cruise ship started to sink.
All are accounted for.
Thirty-two people were hospitalized, officials say, none with critical injuries.
This is NPR News.
Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelensky says the U.S. has raised the idea of a new postwar
security framework for Europe.
This, he warns, could allow Russia to weaken NATO and reshape borders.
The EU yesterday announced it will be part of future peace talks.
Separately, today, Kyiv says Ukrainian forces struck a major Russian oil facility, supporting
Moscow's war effort.
The latest partnership in the visual art world is between the art market website ArtNet and
the prediction market, Kalshi.
Users can wager on whether Andy Warhol's 1986 self-portrait will go for more than $16 million
when it's optioned off next week.
NPR's Anastasia Sulkas reports.
ArtNet started out in 1989 as an online database to provide info on art auction sales.
Last year, it was acquired by venture capital firm Beowulf Capital.
Now, ArtNet says it will help Kalshi curate the markets that users can bet on.
Critics of the deal say that art auctions already take place in a high-stakes, insular
world and that the chances of market manipulation are steep.
Some are also saying it's going to make the art world even more focused on money, not
creative expression.
The partnership was announced soon before the annual wintertime art fairs, like Miami
Art Week, commence.
Anastasia Sulkas, NPR News.
